PST.citation: Gabadinho, A., & Ritschard, G. (2016). Analyzing state sequences with probabilistic suffix trees: The PST R package. Journal of Statistical Software, 72(3), 1-39. doi:10.18637/jss.v072.i03

not_numeric.plot_difference(): draws a heat map or tree of group differences (a ggplot); its numbers come from compare_groups()
not_numeric.plot_distributions(): draws next-state distributions of contexts (a ggplot); the numbers are query_pathway()'s
not_numeric.plot_divergence(): draws the divergence ranking (a ggplot); the numbers are tree_pathways()'
not_numeric.plot_pathway_resamples(): draws bootstrap resample distributions (a ggplot) of bootstrap_pathways()
not_numeric.plot_pathways(): draws the pathway ranking (a ggplot); the numbers are tree_pathways()'
not_numeric.plot_predictive(): draws per-position predictive probabilities or log loss (a ggplot); the numbers are score_positions()'
not_numeric.plot_pruning(): draws a pathway's suffix chain with its G2 keep/prune status (a ggplot); the chain is internal, reachable only by reaching into the plot's data, so its numbers are not compared (API gap, FINDINGS.md)

not_yet.bootstrap_pathways(): resamples sequences inside the function (seed = only) with no argument to supply the resampled indices; a check needs an index argument, or a seeded Monte Carlo study of its stability rates against an established bootstrap
not_yet.as.data.frame.transitiontrees_bootstrap(: the table of bootstrap_pathways(), whose resamples cannot be supplied (see bootstrap_pathways())
not_yet.summary.transitiontrees_bootstrap(): the summary of bootstrap_pathways(), whose resamples cannot be supplied (see bootstrap_pathways())
